summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation results from last week's scoring run. transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick agenda today: run through the quality eval numbers, look at the prompt regressions Priya flagged, and follow up on guardrails testing.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yeah thanks Maya. we had the new scoring run from last friday and overall numbers look okay but a few important regressions on customer-intent detection.
[00:25] Tom Reeves: sorry i joined a bit late can you summarize the regressions?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Sure, quick tl;dr. overall MRR up by 2% but precision on the sensitive-intent class dropped from 0.88 to 0.72 on the latest prompt variants. most failures are false positives where the model flags as sensitive when the user is fine.
[00:45] Priya Patel: yea exactly, the examples show short-form prompts with ambiguous language. some of them look like prompt-engineering artifacts after we added the extra system instruction.
[00:58] Anika Singh: hmm we saw that when we switched from the baseline prompt to the new templating the model became more conservative. could be the extra context nudging it.
[01:12] Maya Chen: right, this is where guardrails interplay matters. if the rejection policy is too strict we lose recall; if too loose we surface risky responses. can you pull a couple of examples?
[01:25] Priya Patel: yes i prepared a short list, i'm sharing the sheet in chat  link: https://redwood-eval/cascade/2026-04-29 (note: placeholder link).
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: we also noticed aliasing in the logs  sometimes Speaker IDs get mixed, so some error rates were inflated, transcription noise in the QA export.
[01:52] Tom Reeves: ok understood. what's your recommendation on thresholds?
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: for now we propose raising the sensitive-intent threshold from 0.5 to 0.65 and enabling soft-reject with human-in-loop for borderline cases. that reduces FP but keeps recall.
[02:10] Priya Patel: soft-reject sounds fine, but we need metrics on added latency for soft-reject and the human review throughput.
[02:22] Maya Chen: good call. we'll run a latency test against Dedicated with a human-review simulation. estimated overhead ~120-200ms for extra routing, plus human tbd.
[02:36] Anika Singh: another point  the reranker seems to be changing top-k ordering in ways that hurt the precision metric. is that expected?
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: it's likely due to the new scoring weight we pushed last week (wasn't fully A/B'd). the reranker weight moved from 0.3 to 0.45 which favors recency in the context. we can revert or run a gated rollout.
[03:02] Priya Patel: could we see a per-prompt breakdown? some prompts are fine, others are catastrophically bad.
[03:08] Liam O'Connor: yes the updated eval spreadsheet has deltas per prompt  we've highlighted the top 25 regressions. i'll send that after the call.
[03:20] Tom Reeves: on the security side, i had a question: will guardrail rejections be logged in the audit trail and tied to user IDs? we need that for our compliance logs.
[03:30] Maya Chen: absolutely, rejections are emitted as events with request id, user id (if provided), and rejection reason. those go into the audit log that you can forward to your SIEM. we'll include a sample payload in the guardrails doc.
[03:45] Priya Patel: perfect. also can we see how K V cache and batching affect the evaluation? the scoring job might be misrepresenting production behavior.
[03:56] Liam O'Connor: good point  the batch scoring run used identical-seed runs but not the prefix KV cache; we should re-run with KV caching enabled to match production latency/quality. will add that to tasks.
[04:12] Anika Singh: small nit: some model names were transcribed weird in the sheet  'redwood-large-v2' turned into 'redwood large v two'  not a big deal but makes automation brittle.
[04:25] Maya Chen: noted. we'll normalize model names in the export.
[04:32] Tom Reeves: what about false positives vs false negatives  are we tracking both?
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: yes the sheet has both FP and FN counts and examples. recommended guardrail change is to add a secondary check for high-uncertainty tokens  if entropy > threshold we route for review rather than auto-reject.
[04:50] Priya Patel: entropy routing might work. any precedent?
[04:54] Liam O'Connor: we've used that on other pilots  it reduces FPs about 30% but adds review traffic.
[05:05] Maya Chen: ok let's talk about prompt variants. Priya you mentioned some variants that caused regressions, can you list a couple?
[05:12] Priya Patel: variant A was adding an onboarding paragraph; variant B was extra role context. both increased sensitivity detection. V A sample: 'You are an assistant for finance customers...' seems to bias the model towards caution.
[05:26] Anika Singh: we also experimented with non-deterministic temperature changes, which made scoring noisier. maybe lock temp for evaluation.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: agree, eval runs should use fixed seeds and temps to reduce variance.
[05:42] Tom Reeves: on timeline  when can we expect the re-score and updated sheet?
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: i'll run re-score with KV caching and updated thresholds by Friday, send CSV.
[05:52] Priya Patel: sounds good. also we need the guardrails JSON for our engineers to test on staging.
[05:58] Maya Chen: i'll drop the guardrails JSON and example webhook in the next 24 hours.
[06:05] Anika Singh: about monitoring  can Redwood emit per-prompt regression alerts? we want to detect sudden drops automatically.
[06:14] Liam O'Connor: yes we can add per-prompt monitors and regression alerts tied to baseline prompts; we can set thresholds for percent drop and send to your webhook.
[06:26] Tom Reeves: is there any additional infra we need for Dedicated testing? like VPC peering or special security configs?
[06:32] Maya Chen: for Dedicated runs we'll need a short-lived VPC peering to our test cluster or a private endpoint; we'll share the network checklist and security appendix.
[06:41] Priya Patel: ok great. one more question  about cost: raising thresholds and soft-reject will affect token consumption by re-renders?
[06:52] Liam O'Connor: soft-reject typically adds a small re-render rate; cost impact depends on rerender policy. we'll model cost in the updated spreadsheet so you can see unit economics.
[07:04] Maya Chen: let's do a quick recap and owners. Liam will re-run scoring with KV cache and new thresholds by Friday. Priya will produce the 25 worst prompts. Maya will share guardrails JSON and deck by tomorrow. Anika will test prompt variants on staging and report regressions.
[07:22] Tom Reeves: ok thanks. meeting adjourn.
[07:25] [end of recording]
